jp: このリンゴ{は|wa-topic}小[ちい]さいです{ね|ne-agreement}。大[おお]きい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}二[ふた]つください。
en: These apples are small, aren't they? Please give me two big ones.
why: 大きい alone cannot be the thing you ask for; の stands in for the apples so you need not repeat the noun.

jp: 靴屋[くつや]{で|de-place}新[あたら]しい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}買[か]いました。
en: I bought a new pair at the shoe shop.
why: 新しい describes shoes that are left unnamed, and の turns it into the new ones.

jp: かばん{は|wa-topic}黒[くろ]い{の|no-pronoun}{と|to-and}白[しろ]い{の|no-pronoun}{が|ga-existence}あります。
en: As for the bags, there are black ones and white ones.
why: 白い needs の to mean white ones, a noun phrase that can then take が before あります.

jp: このメニュー{の|no-possessive}中[なか]{で|de-scope}一番[いちばん]安[やす]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-topic}カレーです。
en: The cheapest one on this menu is the curry.
why: 一番安い names a dish that is not repeated, so の makes it the cheapest one before は.

jp: 父[ちち]{は|wa-topic}辛[から]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-contrast}食[た]べられません。
en: My father cannot eat spicy ones.
why: 辛い stands for spicy dishes, and の makes it a noun that the particle は can follow.

jp: 今日[きょう]{は|wa-topic}暑[あつ]い{から/ので|kara-because}、白[しろ]い{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}着[き]ます。
en: It's hot today, so I'll wear a white one.
why: 白い alone cannot be the object of 着ます; の stands for the white piece of clothing.

jp: 高[たか]い{の|no-pronoun}{より|yori-comparison}安[やす]い{の|no-pronoun}{を/が|tai-ga-o}買[か]いたいです。
en: I want to buy a cheap one rather than an expensive one.
why: 安い becomes the cheap one with の, and that noun phrase is what 買いたい wants as its object.

jp: 野菜[やさい]{は|wa-topic}新[あたら]しい{の|no-pronoun}{が|ga-subject}おいしいです。
en: For vegetables, fresh ones are tasty.
why: 新しい must become a noun phrase (fresh ones) with の before it can be the subject marked by が.

jp: 高[たか]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-topic}千円[せんえん]、安[やす]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-topic}五百円[ごひゃくえん]です。
en: The expensive one is a thousand yen and the cheap one is five hundred yen.
why: 高い and 安い each stand for one of two items, and の makes each a noun that は can mark.

jp: 暑[あつ]かった{ので/から|node-because}、冷[つめ]たい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}飲[の]みました。
en: It was hot, so I drank a cold one.
why: 冷たい stands for a cold drink, and の makes it the noun that を marks as the thing drunk.

jp: この財布[さいふ]{は|wa-topic}使[つか]いにくいです。もっと便利[べんり]な{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}探[さが]しています。
en: This wallet is hard to use. I'm looking for a more convenient one.
why: After a na-adjective the pronoun の is attached to 便利な to mean a more convenient wallet.

jp: 妹[いもうと]{に|ni-recipient}かわいい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}プレゼントしました。
en: I gave my little sister a cute one as a present.
why: かわいい describes the gift without naming it, and の makes it the cute one that is given.

jp: あの靴[くつ]{は|wa-topic}、白[しろ]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-contrast}もうありません。
en: As for those shoes, the white ones are no longer available.
why: 白い means the white pair only after の makes it a noun, which は can then mark.

jp: お金[かね]{が|ga-existence}ない{ので/から|node-because}、高[たか]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-contrast}買[か]えません。
en: I have no money, so I can't buy expensive ones.
why: 高い stands for expensive things; の makes it a noun phrase that は can mark.

jp: うどん{は|wa-topic}太[ふと]い{の|no-pronoun}{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです{が/けど|ga-but}、そば{は|wa-topic}細[ほそ]い{の|no-pronoun}{が|ga-stative}好[す]きです。
en: I like thick udon, but I like thin soba.
why: 太い describes noodles that are left unnamed, so の turns it into thick ones before が.

jp: お土産[みやげ]{は|wa-topic}軽[かる]く{て|te-sequence}小[ちい]さい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}選[えら]びました。
en: As for souvenirs, I chose a light, small one.
why: The adjectives 軽くて小さい describe an unnamed souvenir; の makes them the light, small one.

jp: 今日[きょう]{の|no-possessive}パン{は|wa-topic}昨日[きのう]食[た]べた{の|no-pronoun}{より|yori-comparison}おいしいです。
en: Today's bread is tastier than the one I ate yesterday.
why: 食べた describes the bread of yesterday, and の stands for it so it can be compared with より.

jp: ハンカチ{は|wa-topic}小[ちい]さい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}いつも持[も]っています。
en: As for handkerchiefs, I always carry a small one.
why: 小さい alone cannot be carried; の stands for the handkerchief, giving a small one.

jp: このシャツ{は|wa-topic}高[たか]いです{が/けど|ga-but}、あの白[しろ]い{の|no-pronoun}{は|wa-topic}安[やす]いです。
en: This shirt is expensive, but that white one is cheap.
why: 白い describes the shirt without repeating it, and の makes it the white one that は can mark.

jp: ケーキ{は|wa-topic}小[ちい]さい{の|no-pronoun}{と|to-and}大[おお]きい{の|no-pronoun}{を|o-object}注文[ちゅうもん]しました。
en: As for cakes, I ordered a small one and a big one.
why: 大きい stands for a cake, and の makes it a noun that を can mark as the thing ordered.
